samples.summary: Sibling flat-lookup site `getSelectedTableCells()` was not updated, so the clipboard still cannot see a nested table's cell rectangle that selection.ts now paints
samples.evidence: The diff replaces the flat `layout.blocks.find(...)` in `normalizeRange()` with a `resolveNestedTableLayout()` fallback, but `TextEditor.getSelectedTableCells()` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4269) still does exactly the old thing: `const lb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cr.blockId); if (!lb?.block.tableData) return null;`. A nested table is not in `layout.blocks`, so a cell rectangle inside an inner table yields `null` cells for copy/cut, while the deletion path one screen away (text-editor.ts:4114) resolves the same id through `this.doc.getBlock(cr.blockId)`, which *does* walk into cells. Cut of a nested cell rectangle therefore clears cells (4116-4128) with nothing captured for the clipboard. The change makes this divergence visible/wider because the painted rectangle for the nested case is now merge-expanded while the copy path still bails out entirely. Fix belongs at 4269 (use `resolveNestedTableLayout(cr.blockId, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData` as selection.ts now does).

samples.summary: Mutation paths read the RAW `selection.range.tableCellRange`, not the newly nested-aware normalized one, so paint and write can now disagree for nested tables
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4398 (`applyCellStyle` loop), editor.ts:1294 (`applyStyleToCellRange`), text-editor.ts:2902 (`forEachBlockInSelection`) and text-editor.ts:3709 (`applyStyleToSelection`) all consume `range.tableCellRange` verbatim. The diff adds read-time merge expansion for nested tables in `normalizeRange()` only, so a nested-table cell range that was not expanded at write time (programmatic `Selection.setRange`, or the undo-restore path at editor.ts:2492 which reinstates a stored rectangle verbatim) now paints a larger rectangle than the one these writers mutate. Same class of divergence already existed for top-level tables; the change extends it to nested ones.

samples.summary: The new shift+click cell-range branch only fires for top-level tables, so it does not reach parity with the drag path it claims to mirror
samples.evidence: The new guard is `anchorCellInfo.tableBlockId === pos.blockId`, where `pos.blockId` comes from `this.doc.document.blocks.find(...)` at text-editor.ts:2023 and is therefore always a TOP-LEVEL table. For an anchor inside a nested table, `anchorCellInfo.tableBlockId` is the inner table id, the condition is false, and control falls into the pre-existing `else` at 2104-2107 which clears the selection. The drag path handles exactly this case at text-editor.ts:2399-2417 (`resolvedCellInfo.tableBlockId === anchorTableId` → inner-table cell range), so shift+click and drag remain out of step for nested tables even though the comment claims the gestures now agree. Keyboard shift+arrow (text-editor.ts:3360-3375) also handles the nested case.

verdict.reason: Verified directly in the tree. `getSelectedTableCells()` at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4269-4270 still resolves the cell-range table with the flat `layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cr.blockId)` and returns null when it misses, exactly as quoted. Its updated siblings do not: selection.ts:128-130 now falls back to `resolveNestedTableLayout(crBlockId, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData`, and the adjacent copy path getSelectedBlocks() at text-editor.ts:4316 already uses resolveNestedTableLayout. A nested table is not in `layout.blocks` (selection.ts:121-126 comment; copy-integrity.test.ts:220), and a nested-table tableCellRange is reachable: text-editor.ts:2403-2411 sets `blockId: anchorTableId` for an inner-table cell-range drag. Meanwhile the deletion path at text-editor.ts:4114 resolves the same id via `this.doc.getBlock`, which does walk into cells (document.ts:226-239 -> findBlockInCells), so it clears the whole nested rectangle at 4116-4128. handleCut (text-editor.ts:1460-1470) therefore writes only the anchor cell's sliced blocks (getSelectedBlocks fallback) and then deletes the full rectangle — data loss; handleCopy (1417-1424) silently drops the tableCells payload. Existing coverage is the header top-level table only (copy-integrity.test.ts:1329-1365), not nested. This is an unupdated sibling call site outside the diff relying on the replaced contract, i.e. squarely in the blast-radius lane, and major (silent data loss on cut).
